text: Science is not a pile of facts to memorise. Science is a way of working. It means observing carefully, asking sharp questions, testing what you think you know, and being willing to change your mind when the evidence says you should.

It is in the soil under a mango tree, where organisms too small to see are breaking down fallen leaves. It is inside your own body, where your heart is beating right now without being told to.

Careful observation showed otherwise, and the map had to be redrawn. That correction was not a failure of science. It was science working as it should.

text: And you do not have to do any of it alone. Science has a reputation for lonely geniuses, and it is mostly wrong. Discoveries today come from teams, often spread across many countries, arguing with one another and checking each other's work. Being told you are wrong by someone who has looked carefully at your evidence is not an insult. It is one of the most useful things that can happen to you.
